title: Why your Google Ads “leads” are lying to you
excerpt: The gap between reported leads and booked jobs, and how to close it.
author: Abdul Kader

children.text: Your report says 84 conversions last month. Your office manager says the phone rang maybe thirty times. Both are telling the truth. They’re just counting different things.
This is the single most common problem I find when I open a home service account for the first time. Not bidding. Not ad copy. Counting.

Google Ads reports what it was told to report. If the tag fires on a thank-you page that reloads, on a phone number click that never connects, and on a form that a bot submits at 3am, all three land in the same column. Nobody is lying. The definition is just wrong.
What gets counted as a lead
In a typical account I’ll find duplicate submissions, spam, short calls, phone-number clicks counted as calls, and engagement events quietly set as conversions.
You can do a rough version of this yourself in about twenty minutes. Open your conversion actions and check what each one is actually measuring.
Corrected tracking separates forms, connected calls, WhatsApp clicks, and secondary engagement events so the main lead count means something.
Once the count is real, everything downstream gets easier. Bid adjustments push toward searches that produce work and budget moves to the services that pay.
